claims.text: Controlled heat treatment can induce nanoscale ordered features in equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The induced ordered features may consist of fine precipitates or short-range ordered regions.
A suitable heat treatment can produce the nanoscale ordered features without forming coarse intermetallic phases.
Nanoscale ordered features act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The nanoscale ordered features reduce the dislocation mean free path.
Reducing the dislocation mean free path increases the alloy's hardness.
Reducing the dislocation mean free path increases the alloy's compressive strength.
Reducing the dislocation mean free path increases the alloy's tensile strength.
Heat-treatment-induced nanoscale ordering reduces ductility relative to the simple solid-solution baseline.
The heat-treated alloy has lower machinability than the simple solid-solution baseline.
Avoiding a fully multiphase or coarse-intermetallic microstructure allows the modified alloy to retain moderate ductility and machinability.
Untreated equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength.
The simple solid-solution baseline has favorable plasticity.
The starting as-cast or solution-treated CoCrFeNiTi alloy is in a simple solid-solution state.
The proposed mechanism is limited to quasi-static uniaxial compression or tension between 25 °C and 600 °C.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits precipitate formation, which ordinarily creates an additional phase, while the boundary restricts the hypothesis to a homogeneous single-phase state and excludes alloys with additional phases. The short-range-order branch can satisfy the boundary, but the precipitate branch cannot without further clarification.
